questions.question: Calculate PED if price rises from £10 to £12 and quantity falls from 100 to 80. Is demand elastic or inelastic?
questions.correctAnswer: %ΔP = (12-10)/10 × 100 = 20%. %ΔQ = (80-100)/100 × 100 = -20%. PED = -20%/20% = -1.0. Absolute value = 1 = unit elasticity. Total revenue stays the same.

questions.question: Explain three factors that make demand price inelastic.
questions.correctAnswer: Three factors: (1) Few substitutes (insulin for diabetics). (2) Necessity (bread, electricity, water). (3) Small proportion of income (salt, matches — price changes are insignificant).

questions.question: Evaluate why understanding PED is important for a business setting pricing strategy.
questions.correctAnswer: If demand is inelastic, raise prices — quantity falls less than price rises, increasing revenue. If elastic, lower prices — quantity rises more than price falls, increasing revenue. PED varies by time period, market segment, and price level.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether a government should tax goods with inelastic demand or elastic demand to raise the most revenue. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: taxing inelastic goods raises more revenue (quantity barely falls); taxing elastic goods raises little (consumers switch); equity issue (inelastic goods like energy hit the poor hardest); conclude: tax inelastic goods for revenue efficiency but use revenue to fund progressive spending for equity.
